title: The file that will not shrink
hook: A clever enough zip could make any file smaller. Try fitting eight into seven.

doesNotKnow: that no lossless method can shrink every input

misconception: A clever enough compressor could make any file smaller.
objective: The learner can explain that there are 8 files of 3 bits but only 7 shorter strings, so no lossless compressor can shrink them all; in general 2^n files against 2^n - 1 shorter strings, so shrinking some files means growing others.

claims.source: Each of 3 bits is 0 or 1: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 (000 to 111, all shown on the stage). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): 2^3 = 8; stage FILES lists 000..111.

claims.text: There are only 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 strings shorter than 3 bits: the empty string, 0, 1, 00, 01, 10 and 11.
claims.source: Strings of length 0, 1 and 2 number 2^0 + 2^1 + 2^2 = 7. Checked in node by the builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): 2^0 + 2^1 + 2^2 = 7; stage SLOTS lists empty, 0, 1, 00, 01, 10, 11.

claims.text: Two files cannot share one compressed string: the decompressor would have no way to tell which one was meant.
claims.source: Lossless decompression is a function of the compressed string, so the compressor must be one-to-one (pigeonhole). MacKay, Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms (2003), ch. 4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Derivation: decompression is a function of the compressed string, so two files sharing one output cannot both be recovered; the compressor must be one-to-one. Same counting argument in Sedgewick/Wayne, Princeton COS 226 'Data Compression' lecture ('Impossible to losslessly compress all files'). MacKay ch. 4 passage not opened (no access); the derivation stands on its own.

claims.text: For any length n there are 2^n files of n bits and only 2^n - 1 shorter strings.
claims.source: Sum of 2^k for k = 0..n-1 is 2^n - 1 (geometric series). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Geometric series sum_{k<n} 2^k = 2^n - 1; own node check n = 1..20.

claims.text: A lossless compressor that shrinks some files must make others longer.
claims.source: Counting: if no file of length at most n grows, the 2^(n+1) - 1 files of length at most n map one-to-one onto the 2^(n+1) - 1 strings of length at most n, a rearrangement that keeps total length; so if any file shrinks, another must grow. MacKay (2003), ch. 4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Derivation in the source checked: if no file of length <= n grows, the map is an injection of a finite set into itself, hence a bijection, so total length is preserved and no file can shrink either.

claims.text: Zip works because real files repeat themselves.
claims.source: Dictionary compressors (LZ77, used in zip's DEFLATE) replace repeated substrings with back-references; Ziv and Lempel, 'A universal algorithm for sequential data compression', IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 23 (1977). Statement is about why it works on typical files, not a guarantee. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Zip uses DEFLATE (RFC 1951) = LZ77 back-references to repeated strings + Huffman coding of frequent symbols; Ziv and Lempel, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory IT-23(3) (1977). 'Repeat themselves' is a fair plain-language summary of both parts.

recall.question: A company says its tool makes every possible 1 MB file at least one bit smaller, and gets each one back exactly. Can that be true?
options: Yes, if the method is clever enough
No: there are fewer shorter files than 1 MB files
Yes, but it would be slow
recall.why: There are 2^n files of n bits and only 2^n - 1 shorter strings, so two files would have to share a shorter version and could not both come back.
